title: "Binary compatibility between Bioconductor release and devel"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Binary compatibility between Bioconductor release and devel}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
params:
  old: bioc-release
  new: bioc
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r data}
# All packages in a universe, with the ABI record that r-universe stores for each
# build (computed by abitools): the S4 classes, S4 generics, C functions and
# headers that the package exports, and the ones it imports from other packages, each with a hash.
read_universe <- function(universe){
  url <- sprintf("https://%s.r-universe.dev/api/packages?fields=Version,_abi&limit=99999", universe)
  pkgs <- jsonlite::fromJSON(url, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  names(pkgs) <- vapply(pkgs, function(x) x$Package, "")
  pkgs
}

abi_table <- function(pkgs, field){
  rows <- lapply(names(pkgs), function(p){
    entries <- pkgs[[p]][["_abi"]][[field]]
    if (length(entries))
      data.frame(package = p, key = vapply(entries, function(x) x$key, ""),
                 hash = vapply(entries, function(x) x$hash, ""))
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

# Keys look like "pkg::Class", "pkg::generic:name", "pkg::fun()" or "pkg/include"
abi_type <- function(key){
  ifelse(grepl("/", key), "C header", ifelse(grepl("\\(\\)$", key), "C function",
  ifelse(grepl("::generic:", key, fixed = TRUE), "S4 generic", "S4 class")))
}
types <- c("S4 class", "S4 generic", "C function", "C header")

old <- read_universe(params$old)
new <- read_universe(params$new)
has_abi <- function(pkgs) names(pkgs)[lengths(lapply(pkgs, `[[`, "_abi")) > 0]
common <- intersect(has_abi(old), has_abi(new))

exports <- merge(abi_table(old[common], "exports"), abi_table(new[common], "exports"),
                 by = c("package", "key"), all = TRUE, suffixes = c(".old", ".new"))
exports$change <- ifelse(is.na(exports$hash.new), "removed",
                  ifelse(is.na(exports$hash.old), "added",
                  ifelse(exports$hash.old != exports$hash.new, "changed", "unchanged")))
exports$type <- abi_type(exports$key)

# A removed generic may have moved to another package in devel (e.g. to
# BiocGenerics): a package that exports a generic with the same name in devel,
# but not in release. Other packages may have unrelated generics with that name.
generic_keys <- function(pkgs) grep("::generic:", abi_table(pkgs[has_abi(pkgs)], "exports")$key, value = TRUE, fixed = TRUE)
new_generics <- setdiff(generic_keys(new), generic_keys(old))
moved_to <- function(key){
  if (!grepl("::generic:", key, fixed = TRUE)) return("")
  name <- sub(".*::generic:", "", key)
  to <- sub("::.*", "", new_generics[sub(".*::generic:", "", new_generics) == name])
  paste(setdiff(to, sub("::.*", "", key)), collapse = ", ")
}
exports$moved <- ""
removed <- exports$change == "removed"
exports$moved[removed] <- vapply(exports$key[removed], moved_to, "")
exports$change[removed & nzchar(exports$moved)] <- "moved"

# Release packages that import each export: their binaries were built against the
# release version of the provider.
imports <- abi_table(old, "imports")
dependents_of <- function(keys) sort(unique(imports$package[imports$key %in% keys]))

broken <- exports[exports$change %in% c("changed", "moved", "removed"), ]
broken$dependents <- vapply(broken$key, function(k) paste(dependents_of(k), collapse = ", "), "")
breaking <- broken[nzchar(broken$dependents), ]

exporters <- unique(exports$package[exports$change != "added"])
providers <- unique(exports$package[exports$change != "added" & exports$key %in% imports$key])
changed_pkgs <- unique(broken$package)
breaking_pkgs <- unique(breaking$package)
affected <- dependents_of(breaking$key)

# Packages with an ABI record in only one of the two universes can't be compared.
# This only matters if other packages import their exports.
one_sided <- setdiff(union(has_abi(old), has_abi(new)), common)
one_sided <- intersect(one_sided, intersect(names(old), names(new)))
one_sided_exports <- c(abi_table(old[intersect(one_sided, has_abi(old))], "exports")$key,
                       abi_table(new[intersect(one_sided, has_abi(new))], "exports")$key)
all_imports <- c(imports$key, abi_table(new, "imports")$key)
hidden <- unique(sub("(::|/).*", "", intersect(one_sided_exports, all_imports)))

fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
plural <- function(n, word) sprintf("%s %s%s", fmt(n), word, if (n == 1) "" else "s")
```

## Summary

At each Bioconductor release, every package gets a version bump, so that all
binaries are rebuilt. This is intended to protect against packages breaking when
a package they depend on changes its binary interface (ABI), but it rebuilds all 
packages, including the many that are not affected. We compared the ABI of every package
in Bioconductor release with the same package in devel, to see how many of
these changes actually affect other packages.

- Bioconductor devel has `r fmt(length(new))` packages. Only
  **`r length(providers)`** of them export an interface (S4 class, S4 generic,
  C function or C header) that another package depends on in its binary.
- `r plural(length(changed_pkgs), "package")` changed, moved or removed part of their ABI between
  release and devel. Most of these changes are to interfaces that no other
  package uses.
- Changes in **`r plural(length(breaking_pkgs), "package")`** affect other
  packages: **`r plural(length(affected), "dependent")`** in total
  (`r paste(affected, collapse = ", ")`).

So instead of rebuilding all `r fmt(length(new))` packages, only
`r plural(length(affected), "package")` needed attention. These packages are found
automatically, by comparing the hashes that each binary imports with the current
exports of its dependencies.

## Packages that changed their ABI

```{r changed}
counts <- function(x) table(factor(x, levels = c("changed", "moved", "removed", "added")))
summary_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(changed_pkgs, function(p){
  n <- counts(exports$change[exports$package == p])
  data.frame(Package = p,
             Version = sprintf("%s → %s", old[[p]]$Version, new[[p]]$Version),
             Changed = n[["changed"]], Moved = n[["moved"]], Removed = n[["removed"]], Added = n[["added"]],
             `Affected dependents` = length(dependents_of(broken$key[broken$package == p])),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))
summary_table <- summary_table[order(-summary_table$`Affected dependents`, summary_table$Package), ]
knitr::kable(summary_table, row.names = FALSE)
```

Changed, moved and removed interfaces by type:

```{r types}
by_type <- table(factor(broken$type, levels = types),
                 factor(broken$change, levels = c("changed", "moved", "removed")))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame.matrix(by_type))
```

## Changes that affect other packages

```{r breaking, results = "asis"}
if (nrow(breaking)) {
  knitr::kable(data.frame(Provider = breaking$package, Interface = breaking$key,
                          Type = breaking$type,
                          Change = ifelse(breaking$change == "moved", paste("moved to", breaking$moved), breaking$change),
                          Dependents = breaking$dependents), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("None.")
}
```

When an interface **changed**, rebuilding the dependents fixes them. Not every
change breaks the old binaries: for example, methods keep working when a generic
gets extra arguments. But the hashes do not tell which changes are harmless, and
a rebuild is cheap. When a
generic **moved** to another package, a rebuild fixes dependents that import it
through a package that still provides it (e.g. `import(DelayedArray)`), but not
dependents that import it by name from the old package (`importFrom()`). When an
interface was **removed**, a rebuild can't help: the dependent needs a code
change, which a version bump doesn't provide either.

## Notes

What the changes above mean in practice, checked by hand (November 2026):

| Change | Dependents | Impact |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Biostrings: `MultipleAlignment` classes moved to the new MultipleAlignment package | msa | Real: needed a code change |
| `detail` generic moved from Biostrings to BiocGenerics | ShortRead, HiTC | Real: ShortRead needed a code change (`importFrom(Biostrings, detail)`); HiTC was removed from devel |
| `scale` generic moved from DelayedArray to BiocGenerics | SCArray | Real: a rebuild fixes it |
| `BiocGenerics::table` dispatches on `x` instead of `...` | S4Vectors, IRanges, DelayedArray, R453Plus1Toolbox | Probably real (old methods tables): a rebuild fixes it |
| `enrichplot::upsetplot` gained arguments | ChIPseeker, epiSeeker | Probably harmless: extra arguments don't break methods |
| preprocessCore: `plmrc_wfit()` and `plmrr_wfit()` | affy, affyPLM, oligo | Not a real change: a typo in the declarations in `plmr.h` was fixed, which changed the hash |

## Method

- Data: the ABI records that r-universe stores for each package build in
  [`r params$old`](https://`r params$old`.r-universe.dev) and
  [`r params$new`](https://`r params$new`.r-universe.dev), computed with
  [abitools](https://github.com/r-universe-org/abitools).
- An S4 class's hash covers its slots, superclasses and reference class fields. A C
  function's hash covers its signature (argument and return types), and a header's
  hash covers the contents of the package's `include` directory. An S4 generic's
  hash covers its arguments and the arguments it dispatches on.
- A package imports an interface when it extends an S4 class of another package,
  defines methods for a generic of another package, or links to its C API
  (`LinkingTo`). The dependents of a change are the release
  packages whose binaries import the interface.
- Coverage: a package only has an ABI record if it exports or imports any of
  these interfaces; packages without a record have no binary ties to other
  packages. `r length(common)` packages have a record in both release and devel,
  and these are compared.
  `r length(one_sided)` packages have a record in only one of the two;
  `r if (length(hidden)) paste("the exports of", paste(hidden, collapse = ", "), "are imported by other packages, so changes there are not covered") else "no other package imports their exports, so this does not affect the results"`.
